prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a temple standing today that Henry B. Eyring dedicated or rededicated.
prompts.text_original: A country where Henry B. Eyring dedicated or rededicated a temple now in use (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (dedicated-by column), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Henry B. Eyring dedicated new temples in San Salvador El Salvador (2011) and Paris France (2017), the first temples in both countries. Many of his assignments were rededications of renovated temples, including Buenos Aires (2012), Mexico City and Montreal (2015), Suva Fiji (2016), Idaho Falls (2017) and Tokyo Japan (2022).

answers.name: El Salvador

answers.name: Fiji

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country whose port, coast or island Paul's ship called at or sailed past (Acts 21:1-8; 27-28).
prompts.text_original: A present-day country whose port, coast or island Paul's ship called at or sailed past (Acts 21:1-8; 27-28)
prompts.note: Places in the West Bank or Gaza, such as Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho or Gaza city, count as Palestine, which is not an answer.
prompts.summary: Paul made two long sea journeys late in Acts. First he sailed by Cos, Rhodes, Patara and Tyre to Ptolemais (Acts 21:1-8). Later, as a prisoner bound for Italy, he passed Cyprus, changed ships at Myra and sheltered at Crete before a storm wrecked the ship on Malta. All 276 people aboard reached land safely (Acts 27:37, 44), and the voyage ended at Puteoli in Italy.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: The voyage ended at Puteoli, after Syracuse on Sicily and Rhegium (Acts 28:12-13).

answers.name: Malta
answers.fact: The ship wrecked on Malta, called Melita (Acts 28:1).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: The ships touched Cos and Rhodes and sheltered at Fair Havens on Crete (Acts 21:1; 27:8).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Paul landed at Ptolemais (Acre) and went on to Caesarea, where his later voyage began (Acts 21:7-8; 23:33; 24:27).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Paul changed ships at Patara and again at Myra in Lycia (Acts 21:1-2; 27:5-6).

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: The ship sailed under the lee of Cyprus because of contrary winds (Acts 27:4).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: The ship unloaded at Tyre, and later Paul was let ashore to see friends at Sidon (Acts 21:3; 27:3).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory where Chinese, Rarotongan, Korean, Afrikaans, Thai, Indonesian or Aymara is official.
prompts.text_original: A country or territory where Chinese, Rarotongan, Korean, Afrikaans, Thai, Indonesian or Aymara (Book of Mormon text 1965-1977) is official
prompts.summary: Between 1965 and 1977 the Book of Mormon reached Chinese and Rarotongan (1965), Korean (1967), Afrikaans (1972), Thai (1976), Indonesian (1977) and Aymara selections (1977). Chinese alone serves readers in China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau and Singapore.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: The Korean Book of Mormon appeared in 1967.

answers.name: China
answers.fact: The Chinese Book of Mormon appeared in 1965.

answers.name: Indonesia
answers.fact: The Indonesian Book of Mormon appeared in 1977.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: The Thai Book of Mormon appeared in 1976.

answers.name: Taiwan
answers.fact: Chinese, translated 1965, is Taiwan's official language (Mandarin).

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: The Afrikaans Book of Mormon appeared in 1972.

answers.name: Bolivia
answers.fact: Aymara selections appeared in 1977 and the full text in 1986.

answers.name: Cook Islands
answers.fact: Rarotongan (Cook Islands Maori) got its Book of Mormon in 1965.

answers.name: Hong Kong
answers.fact: Chinese, translated 1965, is official in Hong Kong.

answers.name: Macau
answers.fact: Chinese, translated 1965, is one of Macau's two official languages, with Portuguese.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: Aymara, given Book of Mormon selections in 1977, is co-official in Peru.

answers.name: North Korea
answers.fact: Korean, translated 1967, is North Korea's language.

answers.name: Singapore
answers.fact: Mandarin Chinese, translated 1965, is one of Singapore's official languages.
